locator.text: Display 44.8, p. 44, in the statement of Lemma 4.9

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Unfolding: zeta v X = radialWeight c (log X_a) (log X_b) X = edge c (log X - log X_a) · edge 4 (log X_b - log X) with c = W.controls.activationTime². The paper's page-44 prose sets y_a = log(X/X_a) and y_b = log(X_b/X), which are exactly those two arguments, and c_a = t_1². So on X_a < X < X_b both arguments are positive and the value is exp(-c_a/y_a²)·exp(-4/y_b²); the display's single exponential of the sum is the same number by `Real.exp_add`. Outside, whichever argument is ≤ 0 makes its `edge` factor 0, giving ζ = 0, and Lean adds ζ = 0 for X ≤ 0, where log X is meaningless — a total-function convention, consistent with 'otherwise'. The only non-notational point is that Lean's first cutoff constant is the parameter W.controls.activationTime² rather than a literal t_1²; the paper's c_a is likewise just a positive constant fixed on this page (Proposition C.3 restates it as t_1²).
